label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.5 a.1 co: A thing is GOOD_4 in a given perfection exactly…
locator: I q.5 a.1 co.: Ratio enim boni in hoc consistit, quod aliquid sit appetibile
interpretation: First step of the respondeo's argument that good and being are the same in reality: the notion (ratio) of good consists in something's being desirable, with Aristotle's 'the good is what all desire' (in I Ethic.) as authority. Read per perfection as a biconditional between two distinct predicates, so that the article's conclusion can be stated per perfection as in STMT-GOODNESS-IS-ACTUALITY. Aquinas gives a ratio, which could be formalized as a definition of GoodIn; it is kept a premise so that the conclusion is not analytic relative to a chosen definition (#352). The reply's distinction between good simpliciter and good secundum quid is not formalized.
